Your own estimates are in the model, but none of them sits on the path that decides this comparison, so these figures are still provisional. A share of runs in which an option fitted your goal better than the others is not the chance of reaching your target.

**Switch to GCP leads only provisionally, on Olumi’s unvalidated estimates; your downtime limit of at most two weeks was not tested.**

- **Switch to GCP:** reaches your 20% cost-reduction target in about **29% of model runs**.
- **Stay on AWS:** reaches it in **0% of model runs**, under the no-change assumptions.
- **Phased GCP migration:** has no reported result in this comparison.

The modelled link between GCP workload share and savings is fragile. This is a finding to challenge, not a recommendation: the analysis has not established that switching meets both your conditions.
